stem: Light travels in a __________ line.
solution: Light travels in straight lines, a property called rectilinear propagation of light.

stem: The bouncing back of light from a shiny surface is called __________.
solution: Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it strikes a smooth, shiny surface such as a mirror.

stem: A surface that reflects almost all the light falling on it and forms clear images is a __________.
solution: A mirror has a smooth, polished surface that reflects light regularly to form clear images.

stem: The image formed by a plane mirror is __________.
options: virtual, erect and of the same size as the object
solution: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image of the same size as the object.

stem: In a plane mirror, the image appears to be __________ the mirror as the object is in front of it.
solution: The image in a plane mirror appears as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it.

stem: The left–right reversal of an image seen in a plane mirror is called __________.
solution: Lateral inversion is the apparent left–right reversal of an image in a plane mirror.

stem: A mirror whose reflecting surface curves inward (like the inside of a spoon) is a __________ mirror.
solution: A concave mirror has an inward-curving reflecting surface.

stem: A mirror whose reflecting surface bulges outward (like the back of a spoon) is a __________ mirror.
solution: A convex mirror has an outward-curving reflecting surface.

stem: A concave mirror can form a __________ image when the object is far from it.
solution: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted image of a distant object (and a magnified erect image when the object is very close).

stem: A convex mirror always forms an image that is __________.
solution: A convex mirror always forms a diminished, virtual, erect image, giving a wide field of view.

stem: Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles because they __________.
options: give a wider field of view
solution: Convex mirrors give an erect, diminished image and a wide field of view, useful for rear-view mirrors.

stem: Concave mirrors are used by dentists and as shaving/make-up mirrors because they can __________.
options: form a magnified erect image when the object is close
solution: When the object is close, a concave mirror forms a magnified, erect image, useful for shaving and dentistry.

stem: The bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium to another is called __________.
solution: Refraction is the bending of light when it travels from one medium (e.g., air) into another (e.g., water).

stem: A transparent piece of glass with two curved surfaces used to bend light is a __________.
solution: A lens is a piece of transparent material with curved surfaces that refracts light.

stem: A lens that is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges is a __________ lens.
solution: A convex lens is thick in the middle; it converges (brings together) light rays.

stem: A lens that is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges is a __________ lens.
solution: A concave lens is thin in the middle and diverges (spreads out) light rays.

stem: A convex lens can burn a piece of paper by focusing sunlight because it __________.
options: converges the Sun's rays to a point
solution: A convex lens converges parallel sunlight to a hot focal point that can burn paper — it is a converging lens.

stem: A convex lens is used as a __________.
solution: A convex lens acts as a magnifying glass, forming an enlarged image of a nearby object.

stem: White light passing through a glass prism splits into its component colours. This is called __________.
solution: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its constituent colours by a prism.

stem: The band of seven colours obtained when white light is dispersed is called a __________.
solution: The spread of colours (VIBGYOR) formed by dispersion is called the spectrum.

stem: The seven colours of the spectrum in correct order are __________.
options: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red
solution: The spectrum colours are violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red (VIBGYOR).

stem: A rainbow is formed due to __________ of sunlight by water droplets in the sky.
solution: A rainbow forms when sunlight is dispersed and internally reflected by raindrops, spreading into colours.

stem: White light is actually made up of __________.
solution: White light is a mixture of seven colours, as shown by its dispersion through a prism.

stem: A Newton's disc with the seven colours appears __________ when spun fast.
solution: Spinning a seven-colour (Newton's) disc combines the colours, and it appears whitish, showing white is a mix of colours.

stem: The image formed on a screen that can actually be caught is called a __________ image.
solution: A real image can be obtained on a screen; a virtual image cannot be caught on a screen.

stem: The image formed by a plane mirror cannot be caught on a screen because it is __________.
solution: A plane mirror forms a virtual image, which cannot be obtained on a screen.

stem: Which of the following forms a real, inverted image of a distant object?
solution: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted image of a distant object.

stem: When you write 'AMBULANCE' in laterally inverted form on the front of a vehicle, it is done so that __________.
options: it appears correct in the rear-view mirrors of vehicles ahead
solution: The word is mirror-written so drivers ahead read it correctly in their rear-view mirrors due to lateral inversion.

stem: The reflecting surface of a spoon's inner (curved-in) side acts as a __________ mirror.
solution: The inner, hollow side of a spoon acts like a concave mirror.

stem: A pencil partly dipped in water appears bent at the surface because of __________.
solution: Light refracts (bends) as it passes between water and air, making the pencil appear bent.

stem: Which of the following is used to see objects behind us over a wall, like in a submarine?
solution: A periscope uses two mirrors to see over obstacles, used in submarines and to look over crowds.

stem: The image in a convex mirror is always __________ than the object.
solution: A convex mirror always forms a diminished (smaller) image.

stem: Which of the following statements about a plane mirror image is TRUE?
options: It is erect and laterally inverted
It is inverted top to bottom
It is smaller than the object
solution: A plane mirror image is erect, of the same size, virtual and laterally inverted (left–right reversed).

stem: A magnifying glass is a __________ lens.
solution: A magnifying glass is a convex (converging) lens that forms an enlarged image of a nearby object.

stem: The colour of an opaque object is the colour of light it __________.
solution: An opaque object appears the colour of the light it reflects; the other colours are absorbed.

stem: A red flower appears red because it __________ red light and absorbs the rest.
solution: The flower reflects red light to our eyes and absorbs the other colours, so it looks red.

stem: Which of the following can form both real and virtual images depending on the object's distance?
solution: A concave mirror forms real images for distant objects and a virtual, magnified image for very close objects.

stem: The instrument used to view distant stars and planets uses lenses/mirrors and is called a __________.
solution: A telescope uses lenses and/or mirrors to view distant objects like stars and planets.

stem: A kaleidoscope produces beautiful, changing patterns using __________.
solution: A kaleidoscope uses multiple reflections between mirrors to create symmetric, changing patterns.

stem: A shadow is formed because light __________.
options: travels in a straight line and is blocked by an opaque object
solution: Shadows form because light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through opaque objects.

stem: A concave lens always forms a __________ image.
solution: A concave (diverging) lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.

stem: The Sun appears reddish at sunrise and sunset mainly because of __________ of light by the atmosphere.
solution: Scattering of the shorter blue wavelengths leaves the longer red light, so the Sun looks red at sunrise and sunset.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a mirror with its use?
options: Convex mirror – rear-view mirror in vehicles
Concave mirror – rear-view mirror in vehicles
solution: Convex mirrors are used as vehicle rear-view mirrors for a wide field of view.

stem: Two plane mirrors placed at an angle form __________ images depending on the angle.
solution: Mirrors placed at an angle form multiple images; the smaller the angle, the more images.

stem: The main difference between a real and a virtual image is that a real image __________.
options: can be obtained on a screen; a virtual image cannot
solution: A real image can be caught on a screen, while a virtual image cannot.

stem: Sunlight passing through a small hole into a dark room and forming an inverted image of outside objects illustrates the __________.
options: pinhole camera / straight-line travel of light
solution: A pinhole camera works because light travels in straight lines, forming an inverted image of outside objects.

stem: Which of the following is a converging optical device?
solution: A convex lens (and a concave mirror) converges light; a concave lens and convex mirror diverge it.

stem: The colours we see on a soap bubble or an oil film on water are due to the __________ of light.
solution: Thin films like soap bubbles show colours due to reflection and interference of light, a splitting effect.

stem: The image formed on the retina of the human eye by its lens is __________.
solution: The eye's convex lens forms a real, inverted image on the retina, which the brain interprets as upright.

stem: The splitting of white light by tiny water droplets after rain forms a __________.
solution: Dispersion and reflection of sunlight by water droplets forms a rainbow.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Light' is that:
options: light travels in straight lines and shows reflection, refraction and dispersion, which are used in mirrors, lenses and to explain colours and the rainbow
solution: The chapter explains reflection (mirrors), refraction (lenses), dispersion (spectrum and rainbow) and the straight-line travel of light with everyday applications.

stem: Light travels in a:
solution: Light travels in a straight line; this property is called the rectilinear propagation of light, and it is why shadows and images are formed.

stem: The bouncing back of light when it strikes a smooth, shiny surface is called:
solution: Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it falls on a smooth, shiny surface like a mirror.

stem: The image formed by a plane (flat) mirror is:
options: Virtual, erect and of the same size as the object
solution: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect (upright) image of the same size as the object, at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.

stem: In a plane mirror, the image is laterally inverted, which means:
options: The left and right sides appear interchanged
solution: Lateral inversion means the left side of the object appears as the right side of the image and vice versa in a plane mirror (e.g. the word AMBULANCE is written in reverse on vehicles).

stem: A curved mirror that curves inward (like the inside of a spoon) is a:
solution: A concave mirror is a curved mirror that curves inward (the reflecting surface is on the inner, hollow side); it can form real and magnified images.

stem: A concave mirror is used as a:
solution: A concave mirror is used as a shaving or make-up mirror (it gives a magnified, erect image when the face is close) and in torches, vehicle headlights and reflecting telescopes.

stem: A curved mirror that bulges outward is a:
solution: A convex mirror bulges outward (the reflecting surface is on the outer side); it always forms a small, erect, virtual image and gives a wide field of view.

stem: Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles because they:
options: Give a wider field of view (see more traffic behind)
solution: Convex mirrors are used as rear-view (side) mirrors in vehicles because they give a wider field of view, allowing the driver to see more of the traffic behind, though the images appear smaller.

stem: The bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium to another is called:
solution: Refraction is the bending of light as it travels from one transparent medium to another (e.g. from air to water), because the speed of light changes.

stem: A pencil partly dipped in a glass of water appears bent at the surface because of:
solution: A pencil in water appears bent because light rays from the part in water bend (refract) as they pass from water to air, making the submerged part appear shifted.

stem: A transparent piece of glass with curved surfaces used to bend light and form images is called a:
solution: A lens is a piece of transparent material (usually glass) with one or two curved surfaces that refracts light to form images; the two main types are convex and concave lenses.

stem: A lens that is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges is a:
solution: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges; it converges (brings together) light rays and is also called a converging lens.

stem: A lens that is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges is a:
solution: A concave lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges; it diverges (spreads out) light rays and is also called a diverging lens.

stem: A convex lens can be used as a magnifying glass because it:
options: Converges light and forms an enlarged image when the object is close
solution: A convex lens acts as a magnifying glass — when an object is held close to it, it forms an enlarged (magnified), erect, virtual image, useful for reading small print.

stem: When white light passes through a prism, it splits into its component colours; this is called:
solution: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its seven component colours (a spectrum) when it passes through a prism, showing that white light is made of many colours.

stem: The seven colours of white light (the spectrum) are remembered by the acronym:
solution: White light splits into seven colours — Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red (VIBGYOR / ROYGBIV) — as seen in a rainbow.

stem: A rainbow is formed due to the ______ of sunlight by water droplets in the air.
solution: A rainbow is formed when sunlight is refracted, dispersed and internally reflected by tiny water droplets in the atmosphere, splitting white light into its seven colours.

stem: Objects that allow light to pass through them completely are called:
solution: Transparent objects (like clear glass and water) allow light to pass through them completely, so we can see clearly through them.

stem: Objects that do not allow any light to pass through them are called:
solution: Opaque objects (like wood, metal and a wall) do not allow light to pass through them at all; they form shadows.

stem: A shadow is formed when an ______ object blocks the path of light.
solution: A shadow is formed when an opaque object blocks the path of light travelling in a straight line, creating a dark region behind the object.

stem: Which statement about mirrors is correct? (i) A plane mirror gives a virtual, same-size image (ii) A concave mirror can magnify (iii) A convex mirror gives a wider view
solution: All three are correct: a plane mirror gives a virtual, same-size, laterally inverted image; a concave mirror can form a magnified image; and a convex mirror gives a wider field of view.

stem: The image on which a movie is projected onto a screen is a ______ image.
options: real (can be caught on a screen)
solution: A real image is one that can be caught (formed) on a screen, like the image projected in a cinema; a virtual image (like in a plane mirror) cannot be caught on a screen.

stem: The natural source of light for the Earth is the:
solution: The Sun is the main natural source of light (and heat) for the Earth; the Moon does not produce its own light but reflects the Sun's light.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a mirror with its use? (i) Concave – shaving/headlight (ii) Convex – rear-view mirror (iii) Plane – dressing mirror
solution: All three are correct: concave mirrors are used in shaving mirrors and headlights, convex mirrors as rear-view/side mirrors, and plane mirrors as ordinary dressing mirrors.

stem: The overall importance of studying light is that it helps us understand and use devices like:
options: Mirrors, lenses, spectacles, cameras, microscopes and telescopes
solution: Understanding light and its properties (reflection, refraction) helps us design and use many devices — mirrors, lenses, spectacles, cameras, microscopes and telescopes — that are important in daily life and science.
